title: OPS launch readiness: staffing scenarios & KPI primer
content:
Purpose:
This note is a compact primer for cross-functional launch owners to run quick staffing scenario simulations and track the minimal KPI set needed for a safe ramp. Intended to be short + pragmatic: use in comms with eng leads, SRE, and Ops commander.

Scope / who should read:
- Product Ops lead (owner of this doc)
- Eng release lead + SRE oncall
- Customer Success (first 48h support plan)
- Solutions eng / onboarding for early customers

Quick summary (one-line):
Define 3 staffing scenarios (baseline, surge, catastrophic), map each to the KPI thresholds that trigger scale or rollback actions, and assign owners + slick runbook pointers.

Baseline assumptions (for all scenarios):
- Target initial cohort: internal beta -> 5k MAU (first week), public pilot -> 50k MAU (first month)
- Typical request pattern: 70% short-generation (<128 tokens), 30% long-generation (>512 tokens)
- Model mix: hosted small/medium open model + cached embeddings for search rerank
- SLA target: 99.5% availability, p95 latency < 300ms for short requests

Staffing scenarios (short forms):
1) Baseline (Expected)
   - Ops oncall: 1 engineer (shared SRE rota) per 12h
   - Product/CS: 1 coverage lead weekdays 9–5 PT, escalation to SEs
   - Support tiering: default triage -> product ops -> eng
   - When to escalate: sustained error rate > 1% for 30m or p95 latency > 500ms for 15m

2) Surge (3x traffic above baseline sustained for >2h)
   - Ops oncall: 2 engineers with clear split (infra + serving-runtime)
   - Product/CS: full weekday + weekend standby (rotating)
   - Additional roles: Dedicated on-call for model quality regressions (ML lead)
   - When to escalate to scale/traffic shift: token cost > 1.4x baseline OR per-route queuing observed > 3s

3) Catastrophic (traffic spike >10x or regional outage)
   - Ops oncall: incident commander + 2 SREs + infra lead for region failover
   - Product/CS: Incident communications lead + external comms approvals
   - Actions: immediate traffic shaping, model fallback to smaller quantized variant, open customer status page

Minimal KPI set to track (one view for the commander):
- Availability: % successful requests (rolling 15m, 1h)
- Errors: error rate by class (4xx, 5xx, model-timeout) (15m, 1h)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 by short/long buckets (15m window)
- Token throughput: tokens/sec and per-request token avg (1h)
- Cost rate: $/k request window and predicted daily run rate (24h forecast)
- Queue depth: requests waiting for scheduling (instant)
- Model quality signal: top-level regression metric (prompt set pass rate)

KPI thresholds and proposed immediate actions (owner in parentheses):
- Errors > 1% sustained 30m -> run quick rollback to previous model version; mute nonessential logging (SRE)
- p95 latency short > 500ms for 15m -> enable autoscale policy + increase GPU allocation for serving pool (Infra)
- Token cost burn > 1.4x forecast in rolling 6h -> enact cost-control policy: reduce max tokens, switch heavy routes to cached embeddings (Finance/Product)
- Queue depth > 20 requests for 5m -> apply backpressure on non-critical routes and enable rate-limiter (Serving Runtime)
- Model quality degraded (prompt regression > 5%) -> route traffic to canary-sensitive model variant and open ML triage (Applied ML)

Operational checklist (pre-launch, day-of, first-72h):
- Pre-launch (2 weeks):
  - Confirm autoscale policies and burst capacity knobs (Infra)
  - Pre-warm cache for top 20 prefixes and embeddings (Serving Runtime)
  - Define customer-facing SLO language and incident templates (CS + Legal)
  - Nightly smoke coverage for 7 days across regions (SRE)
  - Load test target: 3x expected peak for 1h with synthetic requests representative of long/short mix (Eng + Perf)
  - Burn-in: run integration test for model fallbacks with network degradation simulations (Applied ML)

- Day-of launch checklist (first 6h):
  - Ops commander on call + standup every 2h for first 6h
  - Live dashboard pinned: availability, p95 short latency, error rate, token burn rate
  - Customer Success ready with templated messages for potential rate limits/slowdowns
  - Activate traffic evolution plan: slow ramp by 20% per hour until 100%
  - Confirm fallback route is reachable and tested (3rd party monitoring check)

- First 72h (stability watch):
  - 8h rolling handoffs, twice-daily syncs across owners (Eng/SRE/Product/CS)
  - Capture top 5 recurring errors and assign immediate remediation tickets
  - Weekly post-mortem if any SLO breached in first 72h

Suggested dashboard columns for a lightweight tracker (sheet-friendly):
- KPI | Current value | 15m trend | Threshold | Owner | Action if breached | Jira ticket
- Example row: p95 short latency | 280ms | +12% | 500ms | Infra | Scale pool + reduce batch size | JIRA-OPS-2899

Quick staffing rota template (examples, copy into calendar):
- Weekday baseline: Ops-A (2–10 PT), Ops-B (10–6 PT), Eng-rotation evening (6–2 PT)
- Weekend baseline: single oncall (10–10 PT) + PD standby (phone)
- Surge uplift: add Ops-C for immediate help and notify infra lead

Comm templates (short fragments to copy into status page / customer comms):
- Internal status blurb: "Investigating elevated latency on generation routes. Immediate mitigations active: autoscale and traffic shaping. Next update in 30m."
- Customer-facing: "We're seeing high traffic which may cause slower responses. We're temporarily limiting some features while we stabilize traffic. Estimated update: 30–60 minutes."

Risks and open questions (notes to self):
- How fast can the model-variant fallback be fully validated in production without incurring a quality regression? (ask Applied ML for automated regression gating)
- Cost alarms are noisy—need better smoothing to avoid false positives on transient bursts
- Customer signaling: need list of priority customers for manual SLA override (sales input)

Immediate next steps (owner tags inline):
- Create the thin dashboard with the minimal KPI columns above (Alyssa)
- Schedule the 2-week pre-launch perf test and invite Perf and SRE (Jordan)
- Draft the default customer message templates and legal-approved wording (Priya)

Notes / scratch:
- This doc is intentionally compact. Expand into the full runbook (link to confluence) once baseline verified in perf test.
- If we decide to use Dedicated capacity for pilot customers, update cost thresholds and staffing rota to include Dedicated SREs.

Appendix: quick triage playbook (cheat-sheet)
- If error rate spikes -> check recent deploys (GitHub PR refs), check model variant change, check infra autoscale events
- If latency increases -> look at queue depth, batch sizes, GPU utilization, network errors to model store
- If cost burn rises -> throttle heavy experimental routes, reduce max tokens, switch to cached embeddings for non-critical queries

End of doc.
